name: Bell 206 JetRanger / LongRanger
summary: The classic light turbine helicopter, flown in huge numbers by US news, police, tour, utility and training operators; the Navy trained helicopter pilots in its TH-57 version until 2025.

wings: Two-blade teetering main rotor on a short mast
engines: Single turbine on the roof behind the rotor mast
Single exhaust stack angled up and aft at the back of the engine cowling
fuselage: Teardrop-shaped cabin with a curved windscreen
LongRanger: stretched cabin with an extra window/door section behind the rear doors
tail: Horizontal stabilizer with small vertical endplate fins
Two-blade tail rotor on a fin with upper and lower (ventral) parts

tellTales: Teardrop cabin on skids with a two-blade rotor and one exhaust stack on top
Horizontal stabilizer with little endplate fins on a slim tail boom
Long slim boom ending in a fin with a lower ventral part

confusedWith.howToTell: The 206 has two main rotor blades; the 407 has four blades on a wider LongRanger-style cabin.
The 505 has a boxy, angular cabin with huge flat windows; the 206 has a rounded teardrop cabin.
The H125 has three blades and a taller, rounder cabin; the 206 has two blades.
The R44 is smaller with a piston engine, tall thin mast and tubular boom; the 206 has a turbine exhaust stack and endplate stabilizer.

usCount.source: FAA registry make/model inquiry (Bell 206A/B/L series and civil OH-58/TH-57)
